column1: # Growth-ratio bounds for the perf grid: how much slower a key op may get
# across each axis of the grid before CI goes red.
# Columns, tab-separated:  <op>  <axis>  <max-ratio>  <why>
# THE `why` COLUMN STARTS WITH ITS OWN CONFIDENCE, MEASURED or PREDICTED,
# exactly as in migration-expectations.tsv and for the same reason: a
# prediction that is never converted is indistinguishable from a measurement.
# Bounds ship PREDICTED; the first run converts them, with its run id, to
# values informed by what was actually measured. The gate itself refuses a
# bounds row whose why carries neither token.
# Axes (defined by named entries in scripts/run-perf-grid.sh's GRID list):
#   claims    (50,4)  -> (800,4):   16x claims, subjects fixed.
#                                   linear ~= 16, quadratic ~= 256.
#   subjects  (800,4) -> (800,400): 100x subjects, claims fixed.
#                                   linear ~= 100, quadratic ~= 10000.
# THE BOUND IS A SHAPE CLAIM, NOT A SPEED CLAIM. Absolute times are reported
# in the run and never judged here: hosted-runner wall-clock varies enough
# that gating on it teaches people to re-run until green. The decade between
# linear and quadratic is wider than any runner's noise; that gap is what a
# ratio can gate and a millisecond count cannot. Ops whose large-end time is
# under 100ms are recorded but not judged (`below-floor` in the gate output).
# A bound a measurement contradicts is corrected by a human, in a commit,
# with the reason here -- the gate's error is the prompt, never the editor.
append
column4: PREDICTED at introduction. Appending to a log should not care how long the log already is (amortized O(1)-to-O(log n)); 8 is half of linear-16, so append drifting toward linear-in-claims trips this before it reaches it.

column1: append
column4: PREDICTED at introduction. Claim count is fixed on this axis; the subject population should be irrelevant to a single append. Same drift argument as the claims-axis row.

column4: PREDICTED at introduction. s0's own claims grow 16x along this axis, so linear is ~16; 32 allows 2x constant drift. The #181 shape (pairwise git subprocesses, ~256) is what this row exists to catch.

column1: show-subject
column4: PREDICTED at introduction. s0's claims SHRINK 100x along this axis (round-robin generation), so the honest expectation is flat-to-faster; 4 flags a read that scales with subjects it did not ask about.

column4: PREDICTED at introduction. The bulk read is the documented fast path (72ms while show-subject took 141s, kan#181) and should stay linear in claims: 16 linear, 2x slack.

column1: show-all
column4: PREDICTED at introduction. Same claim count, more subjects: output volume is unchanged, per-subject bookkeeping is not free but must stay well under linear-in-subjects.

column1: status-all
column4: PREDICTED at introduction. One fold over the log: linear in claims, 2x slack.

column1: status-all
column4: PREDICTED at introduction. Output is one line per subject, so linear-in-subjects (~100) is the honest floor for this op on this axis; 200 is 2x slack over it, and quadratic (~10000) stays two decades away.

column1: issues
